title: Telemetry fanout and multi-window burn-rate synthesis for weighted paging
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current burn-rate alerts operate on a single-window SLI and flood on-call with duplicate pages when a cross-service latency blip affects many downstream services. We need a telemetry fanout layer that synthesizes burn-rate across multiple sliding windows (30s, 5m, 1h) with confidence bands and a weighted paging policy so that short sharp spikes produce low-noise notifications while sustained degradations escalate quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry fanout implemented: ingest path fans metrics/traces into a short-term in-memory windower and a medium-term aggregator
Burn-rate synthesizer computes per-SLI burn-rate across three windows (30s, 5m, 1h) and emits a composite score with confidence bands
Paging policy maps composite score + historical noise profile to pager weight and throttles duplicate alerts for correlated services
Dashboards: latency/error dashboard updated to show multi-window burn-rate bands and service correlation matrix
End-to-end tests + synthetic probe validates that a 20s micro-burst triggers a low-severity ticket while a 10min regression surfaces P1 paging
design_decisions: Use streaming windowing (Apache Flink/ksql style) in the telemetry fanout instead of full-timeseries writes for 30s/5m windows to reduce storage churn
Compute confidence bands using bootstrapped historical baselines per-hour-of-week to account for diurnal patterns
Keep 1h window in centralized long-term TSDB for retrospective analysis but base paging decisions primarily on 30s and 5m synthesized score
Weighted paging uses service importance + traffic correlation; correlation derived from request traces (span parentage) not only topology
Fallback behavior: if trace fanout fails, revert to existing single-window burn-rate to avoid blocking alerts
implementation_notes: New Kafka topic telemetry.fanout.short created; consumer group 'slo-synth' performs windowing and writes composite score to telemetry.slo.composite.v1
Added 2 new metrics: slo.composite_score and slo.composite_confidence (both stamped with window and baseline_tag)
Updated alerting rules in prometheus-rules: slo_burnrate_composite_rate (expr uses slo.composite_score > threshold AND slo.composite_confidence > 0.6)
Introduced deduplication TTL per-correlation-cluster (default 120s) to reduce repeated pages for the same burst
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased telemetry fanout throughput could overload Kafka; Mitigation: throttled producer and producer-side sampling for low-traffic services
Risk: False negatives if confidence bands are overconservative; Mitigation: tune baseline window and enable a canary group with aggressive alerting for 2 weeks
Risk: Pager weight mis-calibration causing missed P0s; Mitigation: manual override and emergency escalation path in console
testing_plan: Unit tests for windowing and composite score logic (edge cases: empty windows, spike at window boundary)
Integration: run telemetry fanout in staging and replay 48h of production trace telemetry to validate noise reduction metrics
Synthetic probes: schedule burst, sustained regression, and slow drift scenarios against staging to validate paging outcomes
Chaos: simulate fanout consumer lag to validate fallback to single-window and ensure no silent alert loss
rollout_steps: Deploy telemetry fanout in canary region with 10% traffic for 72h
Enable composite score consumer and mirror alerts to a shadow slack channel for 1 week
Collect false-positive/false-negative metrics and tune thresholds
Gradual ramp to 100% across regions with monitoring and rollback playbook ready
